newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges release of Chinese labor activists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges release of Chinese labor activists.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday called on China to release two labour activists jailed for 3-1/2 years each for conspiring to subvert the government.

A court in the southern Chinese town of Shenzhen convicted Li Wen-ming and Guo Baosheng on May 30, the Hong Kong-based Information Centre of Human Rights and Democratic Movement in China said in a statement received in Beijing.

"We again urge China to release them," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "They were imprisoned for expressing their political and religious views and we think that they ought to be released."
Li, 28, and Guo, 25, who have been in custody since 1994, are due to be released in November and December this year, respectively.
The New York-based Human Rights Watch group said Li and Guo had tried to educate Chinese migrant workers about their rights to organise and engage in collective bargaining in the workplace.
